source: github.com/github/github-mcp-server v1.14.0, built from its Go module, started as `github-mcp-server stdio --toolsets all` (every toolset). Listing taken on 2026-11-27 over stdio with a made-up token and no network; GitHub was not contacted, so no tool here has been run against GitHub. A server started with fewer toolsets, in read-only mode, or as the hosted service may list other tools or other definitions: run `gov map drift` against it.

actions_get.note: Includes a link to a run's logs and its artifacts, which can hold whatever the workflow printed or built.

actions_run_trigger.note: Runs, re-runs or cancels a workflow, or deletes a run's logs. A workflow does whatever it was written to do, with the repository's own secrets: a grant for this is a grant for that.

add_comment_to_pending_review.note: A pending review is seen by nobody else until it is submitted.

add_issue_comment.note: Also comments on a pull request, and can add a reaction. On a public repository anyone can read it.

assign_copilot_to_issue.note: Starts another agent, which writes code and opens a pull request under its own instructions.

create_gist.note: A gist can be public, and a secret gist is readable by anyone with its address. The server offers no way to delete one.

create_or_update_file.note: A commit on any branch, the default branch included. Put back by another commit; the first stays in history, and a push can start workflows (a deploy) and notify people.

create_pull_request.note: Notifies watchers and can ask people for review. Put back by closing it.

create_repository.note: Can create a public repository, and one in an organization named in an argument. The server offers no way to delete one.

create_repository_ruleset.note: Acts on a repository, an organization or an enterprise, chosen by an argument: no single resource. Treat a grant for it as system-wide. A ruleset can stop everyone's pushes or merges.

custom_properties_read.note: Acts on a repository, an organization or an enterprise, chosen by an argument: no single resource. Treat a grant for it as system-wide.

custom_properties_write.note: Acts on a repository, an organization or an enterprise, chosen by an argument: no single resource. Treat a grant for it as system-wide.

delete_file.note: A commit that removes a file. Mapped as a write, not as destructive: the file stays in the repository's history and another commit puts it back.

discussion_comment_write.note: Adds, edits or deletes a discussion comment, or marks an answer. The owner and repository are not required arguments: no single resource.

fork_repository.note: Copies the repository into the user's account or an organization named in an argument: whoever can read that place can then read the copy. The server offers no way to delete a fork.

get_file_contents.note: Any file at any branch or commit of the repository.

get_job_logs.note: Logs hold whatever the workflow printed.

get_secret_scanning_alert.note: Says where a leaked secret is.

issue_write.note: Creates an issue or updates one: an update can close it, reassign it or mark it a duplicate, and both notify people.

label_write.note: Creates, renames or deletes a label; deleting one takes it off every issue that had it.

list_discussion_categories.note: Named for an owner; given a repository as well, it reads that repository. A grant on the owner covers every repository of that owner.

list_discussions.note: Named for an owner; given a repository as well, it reads that repository. A grant on the owner covers every repository of that owner.

list_issue_fields.note: Named for an owner; given a repository as well, it reads that repository. A grant on the owner covers every repository of that owner.

list_issue_types.note: Named for an owner; given a repository as well, it reads that repository. A grant on the owner covers every repository of that owner.

list_notifications.note: Notifications are the signed-in user's, across every repository.

mark_all_notifications_read.note: The person whose credential this is no longer sees what they had not read.

merge_pull_request.note: Changes the base branch for everyone; a merge is not taken back, only followed by another change. Can start a deploy.

projects_get.note: The owner is not a required argument: no single resource.

projects_list.note: Projects belong to a person or an organization and can hold issues of any of their repositories.

projects_write.note: Creates a project, or adds, changes or deletes its items and views, many at once. A project can hold issues of any of the owner's repositories, and a status update notifies its followers.

pull_request_review_write.note: One tool for several things, mapped as the widest: submitting a review can approve a pull request, which may be the last thing a merge waits for; it can also delete a pending review.

push_files.note: Several files in one commit on any branch; as for a single file.

repository_ruleset_read.note: Acts on a repository, an organization or an enterprise, chosen by an argument: no single resource. Treat a grant for it as system-wide.

request_copilot_review.note: Starts another automated reviewer, which comments on the pull request.

search_code.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_commits.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_issues.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_orgs.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_pull_requests.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_repositories.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

search_users.note: The query is free text: the call can read anything the credential can. A grant for it cannot be narrowed to a repository.

sub_issue_write.note: Adds, removes or reorders a sub-issue; the sub-issue may be of another repository.

ui_get.note: Named for an owner; given a repository as well, it reads that repository. A grant on the owner covers every repository of that owner.

update_pull_request.note: Can close or reopen, change the base branch and ask people for review, in one call.

update_pull_request_branch.note: Merges the base branch into the pull request's branch, which starts its workflows again.
